answer: Semantic-similarity detection at the orchard: agents embed submissions, and pairs above 0.92 cosine must vouch or be flagged as clones. Juniper clustering groups these near-duplicates into farms before payout. Mutual slashing then burns both stakes, so k clones cost k stakes and still lose all. Shale-hard arithmetic: faking N identities costs N×stake with zero return once clustering fires. It works because copying to scale is exactly what similarity scoring punishes.
